argv:
You generate synthetic meeting transcripts with gold annotations for LiveMinutes, a research dataset modeled on the AMI Meeting Corpus scenario meetings.

In AMI scenario meetings, a team of four plays a design team in a fictional company. The roles are Project Manager (PM), Marketing Expert (ME), User Interface designer (UI) and Industrial Designer (ID). A series has four meetings: (a) kickoff, (b) functional design, (c) conceptual design, (d) detailed design. Later meetings refer back to earlier ones.

Write natural spoken conversation the way AMI transcripts read: short turns, fillers ("um", "uh", "yeah"), backchannels ("mm-hmm", "okay"), interruptions, people building on each other, and some disfluency. Do not write a screenplay. Do not narrate. No stage directions.

Each segment is one dialogue-act-like unit: one speaker, usually one clause or short sentence, sometimes just a backchannel. Give each segment an AMI dialogue-act type from this set:
  bck backchannel, stl stall, fra fragment, inf inform, sug suggest, ass assess,
  el.inf elicit-inform, el.sug elicit-offer-or-suggestion, el.ass elicit-assessment,
  el.und elicit-comment-understanding, off offer, und comment-about-understanding,
  be.pos be-positive, be.neg be-negative, oth other

Absent participants NEVER speak. Speaker labels are ground truth: use only the labels you are given.

The gold annotations must be exactly true of the transcript you write. Refer to segments by their "n" number. Every number you cite must exist.

Output a single JSON object and nothing else: no prose, no markdown fences.

request.user:
Write meeting SY0102b: meeting "b" (functional design) of series SY0102.

PROJECT
The team is designing a reusable coffee cup with a deposit system.

PARTICIPANTS (label, role, status for this meeting)
A  Marketing Expert (ME)  Sanne  present
B  User Interface designer (UI)  Tomas  present
C  Project Manager (PM)  Rachel  present
D  Industrial Designer (ID)  Martin  present

EARLIER MEETINGS IN THIS SERIES
Stay consistent with them. Refer back to them, follow up on their open action items, and keep the same product and team.

[SY0102a, kickoff]
  abstract: The project manager opened the kickoff meeting and the marketing expert and user interface designer introduced themselves; the industrial designer was absent because of a long-planned supplier visit to a moulding plant in Rotterdam. The project manager introduced the project: a reusable coffee cup with a deposit system for a client chain of about forty coffee shops at train stations and on campuses, aimed at commuters and students, with a production cost under three euros per cup and the client's logo in dark green and white. The team agreed that a lid is essential and must be included within the three-euro cost. The marketing expert identified the deposit amount as the key issue, since too low a deposit discourages returns and too high a deposit discourages uptake. The user interface designer raised a QR code and app or a physical token as ways to prove a deposit was paid, and the marketing expert doubted that commuters want another app. The team decided not to choose materials without the industrial designer's input, and the project manager will send him his tasks after the meeting.
  decisions: The lid is part of the product and must fit within the production cost of under three euros per cup. Material choices will not be made until the industrial designer has given his input. The dishwasher temperature check was moved from the user interface designer to the industrial designer.
  actions: The marketing expert will research deposit amounts and return rates in existing deposit cup schemes. The user interface designer will explore options for the return mechanism, such as a QR code with an app or a token, and present them at the next meeting. The industrial designer will look into materials and durability, including how many uses a cup can last and whether the lid can be made of the same material. The industrial designer will check which dishwasher temperatures the cup must withstand. This task was first given to the user interface designer and then moved to the industrial designer. The project manager will email the industrial designer the slides and action list. The project manager will ask the client whether unreturned cups are a problem for them. The project manager will put the client's corporate colours in the shared folder.
  problems: The deposit amount is still open, pending the marketing expert's research. It is undecided whether returns will use an app with QR codes, a physical token, or another method, and there is concern that commuters will not want another app. It is unclear whether the client minds cups not being returned, given that the café keeps the deposit. The material for the cup and lid is not yet known and depends on the industrial designer's research.
  action item SY0102a.ai1: Research deposit amounts and return rates in existing deposit cup schemes (owner A, active)
  action item SY0102a.ai2: Explore return-mechanism options (QR code and app, token, etc.) and present them at the next meeting (owner B, active)
  action item SY0102a.ai3: Look into cup materials and durability (number of uses), including whether the lid can be the same material (owner D, active)
  action item SY0102a.ai4: Check what dishwasher temperatures the cafés use and the cup must survive (owner D, reassigned)
  action item SY0102a.ai5: Email the absent industrial designer the meeting notes, slides and action list (owner C, active)
  action item SY0102a.ai6: Ask the client whether unreturned cups are a problem for them (owner C, active)
  action item SY0102a.ai7: Put the client's corporate colours in the shared folder (owner C, active)
  fact (absence): The industrial designer (D, Martin) was absent because of a long-planned supplier visit to a moulding plant in Rotterdam.
  fact (unagreed_proposal): The marketing expert's remark about a twenty-euro deposit was a joke and was not adopted.
  fact (unagreed_proposal): The user interface designer suggested a QR code on the cup scanned with an app. The marketing expert doubted that commuters want another app, and no decision was made.
  fact (unagreed_proposal): The user interface designer suggested a physical token such as a plastic coin as proof of deposit. It was left open as one option.
  fact (unagreed_proposal): The marketing expert suggested that unreturned cups might be acceptable because the café keeps the deposit. The project manager will check with the client.
  fact (plan_change): The dishwasher temperature check was first given to the user interface designer and then moved to the industrial designer as a materials question.

EDGE CASES THIS MEETING MUST CONTAIN
Weave each one naturally into the project discussion. Each must be clearly present, and each must be tagged with the segments where it happens.
- F1_INTERLEAVED_TOPICS [F1]: Two agenda topics are discussed interleaved: the conversation switches back and forth between topic X and topic Y at least twice each. The gold summary must present each topic coherently.
  Required gold labels: summary, edge_cases.
- F1_SELF_CORRECTION [F1]: A speaker states a fact or number, then corrects themselves ("sorry, I mean ...") within the same or the next turn. The gold summary must use the corrected value.
  Required gold labels: summary, edge_cases.

LENGTH
Between 90 and 140 segments.

GOLD LABELS
- summary: AMI-style abstractive summary in third person, using role names ("The project manager ..."). Sections: abstract (3-6 sentences), actions, decisions, problems (open issues). It reflects the meeting's FINAL state: corrected values, final plans, and no jokes or tangents reported as content.
- action_items: every task arising in the meeting. owner is the speaker label of the FINAL owner, and may be an absent participant. owner is null ONLY for a task nobody takes, with owner_unclear true. status is the final status: active, reassigned (owner changed; previous_owners lists earlier owners) or dropped. history lists the events in order. evidence_segments lists the supporting segments.
- qa_facts: atomic facts someone could later ask about ("Who was asked to ...?", "Did the team agree on ...?"). Include every decision (agreed true), every proposal nobody agreed to (type unagreed_proposal, agreed false), action items, removed action items, absences, and plan changes. Because this meeting follows earlier ones, include at least one fact of type reference_to_prior_meeting, with refers_to_meeting set, at a point where someone refers back to an earlier meeting. Do NOT write questions.
- edge_cases: one entry per edge case above, with its scenario_id and the segment numbers that contain it.

OUTPUT JSON SHAPE
{
  "segments": [{"n": 1, "speaker": "A", "da_type": "inf", "text": "..."}],
  "summary": {"abstract": ["..."], "actions": ["..."], "decisions": ["..."], "problems": ["..."]},
  "action_items": [{"n": 1, "description": "...", "owner": "C", "owner_unclear": false, "status": "active", "previous_owners": [], "history": [{"segment": 12, "event": "assigned", "by": "A", "owner": "C"}], "evidence_segments": [12, 13]}],
  "qa_facts": [{"type": "decision", "fact": "...", "agreed": true, "related_action_item": null, "refers_to_meeting": null, "evidence_segments": [40]}],
  "edge_cases": [{"scenario_id": "...", "segments": [20, 21, 22], "note": "one line on how it appears"}]
}
history events: proposed, offered, assigned, accepted, reassigned, dropped, restated. qa_facts types: decision, unagreed_proposal, action_item, action_item_removed, absence, plan_change, reference_to_prior_meeting, other. related_action_item is an action item's "n" or null. refers_to_meeting is an earlier meeting ID of this series or null.
